a shift toward a smaller hemithorax indicates volume loss (hypoplasia/atelectasis), whereas a shift away suggests a space-occupying lesion (mass/effusion).", "Inspect the lung parenchyma for signs of hypoplasia, such as lobar aplasia, reduced vascular markings, or anomalous venous drainage (e.g., scimitar vein), rather than acute consolidation or large fluid collections.", "Differentiate between primary volume loss causing the shift versus secondary compensatory hyperinflation of the contralateral lung pushing the mediastinum;
